transcript.content: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. Thank you for coming in today. What brings you to see me?

Hello, Doctor. I'm here because... well, I just can't stop seeing this droop and unevenness around my mouth and jaw. It's all I can look at in every single photo and reflection. 

Even when people tell me I look fine, it just feels so obvious to me. It's actually gotten to the point where I've started avoiding presentations at work, and I'm even backing out of meeting with my clients. I just don't want anyone looking at me.
Have you seen a doctor or dermatologist about this concern with your mouth and jaw, or have you considered any cosmetic procedures to address it?

No, I haven't... I haven't actually gone to a dermatologist or a plastic surgeon or anything like that. I mean, I guess the thought of getting it fixed crosses my mind because I hate how it looks so much, but... no, I haven't looked into any specific cosmetic procedures or seen a medical doctor about it yet.
Have you ever had a doctor, dermatologist, or anyone in the medical field actually examine your mouth and jaw to tell you whether there's a real problem there?

No, I haven't. Like I mentioned a moment ago, I haven't been to any kind of doctor or specialist for this. Nobody has actually examined my face or... or told me if there's a medical issue going on. I just know what I see when I look at myself.
Have you repeatedly asked friends, family members, or anyone else to look at your mouth and jaw or to reassure you about whether it looks abnormal?

Yes, I do. I ask my husband constantly if my face looks lopsided. But it really goes beyond just asking him. 

Before work or... well, really any family event, I can spend hours just checking the bathroom mirror. I take pictures on my phone from all these different angles to see how bad the droop is. I'll redo my makeup over and over, or try to adjust my scarf to hide my jawline. And then I usually end up scrolling through photos of other women online, just to see how bad my face looks compared to theirs. It just takes up so much of my time.

You mentioned you've been avoiding presentations at work and backing out of meetings with clients because of this concern about your face. How much has this preoccupation with your mouth and jaw affected your ability to do your job or maintain your relationships?

It's affecting everything, honestly. I actually cancelled a major client presentation at the last minute recently because I just... I couldn't face being seen by all those people. As an architect, networking and presenting is a huge part of my job, but I've been skipping out on events, even award-related ones, because of it. My project deadlines are slipping. And it's not just work... my family gatherings are starting to fall apart around this, too. I just can't bring myself to go out and let people look at me.

When your husband looks at your mouth and jaw, what does he actually say? Does he tell you that he can see the droop and unevenness that you're describing, or does he say he doesn't notice anything wrong?

He always tells me I look fine. He says he doesn't see any droop or unevenness at all. But... I mean, I'm here because I just can't stop seeing it. Every time I look in a mirror or see a photo, it's right there. It's so obvious to me, no matter what he says, and it's gotten to the point where, like I said, I'm avoiding my clients and skipping presentations. His reassurance doesn't change what I see.
How long have you been preoccupied with the way your mouth and jaw look? When did this first start bothering you?

I'm not exactly sure, honestly. Um... it feels like it's been a long time. I can't really pinpoint the exact month or year it first started bothering me. It just... it seems like it's been on my mind for quite a while now, and it's just gradually taken over everything.
Have you ever actually gone through with any cosmetic procedures, treatments, or surgeries to try to fix the droop or unevenness you see in your mouth and jaw?

No, I haven't. I haven't had any surgeries or treatments or anything like that. I've definitely thought about it... a lot, actually. But I haven't actually gone through with any procedures to try and fix it.
Besides your mouth and jaw, are there other parts of your body or appearance that you find yourself frequently worrying about or checking in the mirror?
No, not really. It's just... it's just my mouth and my jaw. That's the only thing that bothers me. I don't really focus on anything else.
